Indian benchmark indices ended higher for the fourth straight session on September 21.

The Sensex was up 564.03 points or 0.76 percent at 74,858.99, and the Nifty was up 67.90 points or 0.29 percent at 23,414.30. About 2086 shares advanced, 2177 shares declined, and 198 shares were unchanged.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Up)
GIFT Nifty was trading higher at around 23,515.50 in early trade, indicating a positive start for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Equities (Up)
Asian stocks rose in early trading as the region’s heavyweight technology shares tracked US peers higher on optimism around Meta Platforms Inc.’s new artificial intelligence agent.
MSCI Inc.’s gauge of Asian shares climbed 0.5%, with memory chipmakers Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. the top contributors to gains.
South Korea’s benchmark Kospi Index jumped more than 2%. Contracts for US benchmarks edged higher after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 posted their best days since early August.
US Equities (Gain)

The Nasdaq surged to a record-high ​close on Monday, lifted by gains in Advanced Micro Devices and other AI heavyweights, while Treasury yields retreated from recent highs and ‌crude prices tumbled to an 11-day low on speculation about a potential breakthrough in Middle East talks at a UN meeting this week.
The S&P 500 climbed ​1.49% to end the session at 7,764.70 points. The Nasdaq gained 2.26% to 27,122.09 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.71% to 52,048.83 points.
Dollar Index (Up)
The US dollar index (DXY) was around 100.3, holding near a seven-week high, supported by expectations of further US Federal Reserve rate hikes.
Asian Currencies (Gain)

Asian currencies traded mostly higher against the US dollar, with the South Korean won rising the most by 0.888%, followed by the Taiwan dollar (+0.234%) and Philippines peso (+0.198%). The Thai baht (+0.087%), Malaysian ringgit (+0.064%), Chinese renminbi (+0.036%) and Singapore dollar (+0.016%) also gained marginally. Meanwhile, the Indonesian rupiah fell 0.499%, while the Japanese yen slipped 0.013%.
Crude (Gains)
Oil prices gained on Tuesday as the market steadied after several days of declines, with investors awaiting developments on potential US-Iran talks at the United Nations General Assembly this week.
The Brent crude futures November contract gained 22 cents, or 0.22%, to $100.57 a barrel. The WTI October contract, which expires on Tuesday, crept up 2 cents, or 0.02%, to $95.8 a barrel.
Gold (Up)
Gold edged higher as a slump in oil prices over the past few sessions reduced the chance of further interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve to contain inflation.
Bullion was trading around $4,360 an ounce, reversing course after falling the most in a week the day before.
Fund Flow Action
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold equities worth ₹576 crore on September 21, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) bought equities worth ₹2,800 crore during the session.
